page: Amazon Web Services c5n.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 21.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 2.62 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory tasks. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 8394.73 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1167.0, both falling into the average tier. Multi-core performance is relatively weaker, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4460.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 27.94 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is stable, measuring 49.97 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations. For specialized workloads, the instance handles static web serving at 6.37 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 7.25 million operations per second. However, LLM inference performance is limited, with prompt processing on a 7B model dropping to a poor tier of 12.14 tokens per second.

The c5n.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for network-intensive compute workloads, supported by a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The absence of local storage requires reliance on EBS, which may introduce latency tradeoffs depending on the storage configuration. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and DDR4 memory speed provide reliable, predictable performance for medium-scale applications without the premium cost of GPU-accelerated or high-memory instances. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose network-bound compute tasks.
